Look for Portugal on this map of Europe in 1600. You won't find it. Here is the continent at the height of the age of empires.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ From 1580 to 1640 one Habsburg king ruled both Spain and Portugal. Portugal kept its own institutions, but the whole peninsula and two global empires answered to Philip II and then his son and grandson.

2/ It ended on 1 December 1640, when Portuguese nobles rose up and backed John IV of the House of Braganza. The union had also made Portugal's colonies a target for Spain's enemies, above all the Dutch.

3/ The giant in the middle is the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. At its early-1600s peak it covered roughly 1 million km² and around 12 million people, with an elected king and a powerful parliament of nobles.

4/ Its eastern neighbour was falling apart. Russia's Time of Troubles began in 1598 when the Rurik line died out. A Polish garrison held the Moscow Kremlin until October 1612, and the Romanovs took the throne in 1613.
5/ The future was being drafted elsewhere too. Elizabeth I granted the English East India Company its charter on 31 December 1600, and the Dutch founded their own company, the VOC, in 1602.
6/ And in Rome, on 17 February 1600, the philosopher Giordano Bruno was burned at the stake in the Campo de' Fiori. He had argued that the stars are distant suns with planets of their own.
Which power on this map had the best long-term prospects in 1600? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
